plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: Raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples: 6 lesional AD vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) are profiled with one flagged outlier (sample_01, library size ~4x below median). Step 1 runs QC on the count matrix, confirms the library-size shortfall for sample_01, and decides — via diagnostic plots (PCA, library size, sample correlation) rather than assumption — whether it is a low-depth-but-valid sample to keep (with size-factor normalization correcting for depth) or an outlier to exclude, documenting the decision and testing DE results with/without it as a sensitivity check if kept. Step 2 runs DESeq2 differential expression between AD lesional and control on the raw counts, using the QC decision from step 1, producing a full gene-level results table (log2FC, p, padj) and diagnostic plots (volcano, MA). Step 3 takes the ranked/significant gene list into hallmark pathway enrichment (GSEA-style ranked test and/or ORA on significant genes) against the human MSigDB hallmark gene sets to answer which hallmark pathways change between conditions. This directly answers both parts of the research question — which genes and which hallmark pathways differ — while explicitly handling the shallow sample rather than silently including or excluding it.
